svg.title: warp addresses
svg.text: One warp = 32 lanes, one load instruction: how many 128-byte lines?
memory is row-major: a row of 32768 floats is 1024 lines of 32 floats. Lanes 0–31 = consecutive threadIdx.x
mm_naive: lane i → row₀ + i, all at the same k (reading A[row][k])
32 rows of A (8 of each row's 1024 lines shown); each lane's float is in a different row
mm_coalesced: lane i → col₀ + i, same row k of B (reading B[k][col])
row k of B in memory: the warp's 32 floats fill exactly one 128-byte line
Same arithmetic, 10.9× faster (140,486 → 12,927 ms): the only change is lines 62–63, which swap which index
threadIdx.x drives. In mm_coalesced all 32 lanes also read the SAME A[row][k]: one broadcast, not 32 loads.
animated: naive lanes fire one by one, each into its own row (a new line each time); coalesced lanes land side by side in one line
